evidence: This structure exemplifies a unique architectural style known as "Indochinois," blending elements of French colonial design with traditional Vietnamese aesthetics. In 1958, the museum was acquired by the government of North Vietnam and officially opened its doors to the public on September 3, 1958.
The exhibition area spans more than 2,200 square meters, with exhibits displayed in chronological order. The museum’s exhibits are divided into four primary sections.

The museum also houses a stele inscribed with an ancient dedication to God Harivamsesvara, discovered during an archaeological excavation. To enhance public understanding of Vietnam’s historical narrative, the museum organized an exhibition in Austria and Belgium from September 2003 to November 2004, featuring 450 artifacts, including 416 from 13 Vietnamese museums and 34 from 8 European institutions.
